units: Targ. O. Ex. VII, 28. Targ. Y. II ib. XXI, 18; a. fr.—תשמיש (ד)ע׳ sexual connection. Targ. Y. II ib. XIX, 15 (Y. I דעָרִיס).

Targ. II Sam. III, 31 bier.—
<cite ref="Nedarim 56b:2">Ib.</cite> <he>ע׳ דצלא</he> a bed with a leather mattress.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>ע׳</he> (<cite ref="T00152"><he>רבתי</he></cite>) <cite ref="Q00474"><he>פחיתא</he></cite> a broken bedstead.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 22a:12">B. Bath. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>לעַרְסֵיה וכ׳</he> waiting for the bier of R. A.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3:15">Y. Kil. IX, 32ᶜ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3:15">Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵇ</cite> <he>יהבון עַרְסִי וכ׳</he> place my bier (coffin) at the sea-shore; a. fr.—Pl. <he>עַרְסָן</he>, <he>עַרְסָתָא</he>, <cite ref="P01406"><he>עַרְסִין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 6:4">Targ. Am. VI, 4</cite> <he>עַרְסַתְהוֹן</he> ed. Lag. (oth. ed. <he>עַרְסֵיהוֹן</he>). Lam. R. l. c. <he>אתקין … עַרְסָאתָא</he> he prepared for them four beds.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 5:3">Lev. R. s. 5</cite> (transl. <he>מטות שן</he> Am. l. c.) <he>ע׳ דפיל</he> ivory bedsteads.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:1:8">Y. Ber. III, 6ᵃ</cite> top <he>ע׳ קיסרייתא וכ׳</he> Cæsarean bedsteads which have holes for the girths; a. e.

senses.gloss: (cmp. עָרִיס I) arcade along a row of buildings, sidewalk.
units: <cite ref="Gittin 6a:17">Gitt. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>מצריך מע׳ לע׳</he> required identification of signatures on documents brought from one side of the street to the other.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:7:2">Y. Bets. I, 60ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>מע׳ לע׳</he> from one side of the street to the other (or from one couch to the other, v. <cite ref="I00616"><he>טְעַן</he> II</cite>).—Pl. <he>עַרְסָתָא</he>.

<cite ref="Eruvin 26a">Erub. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>מערב</he> … <he>ע׳ ע׳</he> Ar. (Ms. M. <he>ערסא ערסא</he>; ed. <he>עַרְסְיָיתָא</he>, fr. <cite ref="P01407"><he>עַרְסִיתָא</he></cite>) provided the whole town of M. with ‘Erubs (v. <cite ref="P00680"><he>עֵירוּב</he></cite>), one for each row of connected houses.
